attempts.label: DANDI:001702
attempts.paper_title: Degradation of perineuronal nets in hippocampal CA2 explains the loss of social cognition memory in Alzheimer's disease
attempts.entry_title: CA2 perineuronal nets and social memory in 5XFAD mice (Chaunsali et al. 2025)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Chaunsali, Li, Fleischel et al. (2025) on dandiset 001702. The dandiset's NWB files hold only metadata, with no images or measurements, and its behaviour videos carry no subject, group or trial labels, so the immunohistochemistry and behaviour claims are blocked. The bulk RNA-seq claims of Figure 4 are tested on the counts the authors deposited in GEO (GSE317499), with pydeseq2 and a pinned Gene Ontology release.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Chaunsali et al. (2025) from dandiset 001702 and GEO GSE317499

outcomes.statement: At 3 M, CA2 PNN area coverage does not differ between 5XFAD and control mice.

outcomes.notes: Needs per-slice WFA and PCP4 masks of the Figure 1 CA2 images at 3 to 12 M. The dandiset's 481 NWB files (185,480 bytes each) hold only file-level metadata (identifier, session description, keywords, subject); acquisition, processing, analysis and stimulus are empty in every file (data check, cell tagged sanity). findings.statement: None of the 481 NWB files holds data. Each is 185,480 bytes and holds only file-level metadata (identifier, session description, keywords, subject); acquisition, processing, analysis and stimulus are empty. The identifiers name the original image files of Figures 1, 3, 5 and S1 to S6 and S9, but no image, ROI, table or measurement is deposited, although the description says the dandiset includes immunohistochemical imaging data quantifying PNN integrity. All 22 IHC claims of the paper are blocked.

The 175 behaviour videos are MP4 files outside NWB, named only by figure panel and trial number. They carry no subject, genotype, treatment, DPI or trial-type (Novel 1, Familiar, Novel 2; familiarization or test) label, several arenas share each video, and the counts do not match the paper's mice (for example 15 videos for the 16 mice of Figure 2B, 33 for the 26 of Figure 5E). The scored interaction and exploration times are not deposited. None of the 19 behaviour claims can be tested.

The object recognition videos are deposited four times, under Fig 2I, Fig 2J, Fig 2K and Sup Fig 7 (byte-identical by SHA-256), and in each set Trial 6 and Trial 7 are the same file: 28 assets hold 6 distinct recordings.

The description says the dandiset includes bulk RNA-sequencing data with associated metadata; it holds none, and the counts are in GEO GSE317499 only. The description also keeps a placeholder sentence naming GEO accession "GSEXXXXX" next to the one naming GSE317499.

The NWB subject is a group label, not an animal (82 subject_ids for 481 files, up to 31 files sharing one, such as 5xFAD+_6M_Fig1), so slices cannot be grouped by mouse, which the paper's per-mouse tests (Figure 5I) and five mice per group (Figure 1) need. Sex is U in 476 of 481 files, and session descriptions give the region as Unknown.

Question for the paper's authors: which DESeq2 design gave the DEG counts of Figure 4B and 4C (one model per age, or one model on all 16 samples with contrasts), and were fold changes shrunken before the |log2FC| > 1 cut? One model per age reproduces 95 and 136 at 3 M (98 and 137 with independent filtering at 0.05 in place of R's 0.1); one model on all samples gives 51 and 141. And which enrichment tool, background, term-size limits and GO release gave Figures 4D to 4G? The number of learning and memory terms in the 3 M top 10 is 0 to 3 depending on these choices, and an ECM term reaches adjusted p < 0.05 in one of 16 readings. Three claims are blocked on these choices.

In GEO GSE317499, sample GSM9473154 (3 Month, 5xFAD negative, rep2) has library name 20790 while its run name carries 20690; the count matrix column (M3_5xFAD-10) matches it by sample number, age and genotype.

verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The first executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier queried the archive API and tested the helper's DEG, enrichment, z-score and term-pattern functions on synthetic inputs. It gave its own outcome for each claim. Its other points: the GEO library name 20790 of GSM9473154 against run name 20690 (already a finding), and the background (a) and Cauchy-prior shrinkage choices, which it found reasonable; neither changed anything. It also noted that the fig4c down-count tolerance of 0.6 requires exactly 6 genes, a point about the claims file, which is not changed.

disagreements.reason: The four readings disagree (cell 13). (a)(c) gives 98 up / 137 down, both within tolerance, so reproduced. (b)(c) gives 51/143, so partially reproduced. (a)(d) gives 91/45 and (b)(d) 38/37: more up than down, so not reproduced. Cell 10 says (b)(c) is adopted where the readings disagree; that is the author's own rule, and the claims file's READINGS rule makes a claim methods_underspecified when readings disagree (problem 1). pydeseq2's DeseqStats defaults to alpha 0.05 for independent filtering where R results() defaults to 0.1 (problem 2).

With the 10 to 500 term-size limit, the top 10 hold 3/3, 0/0, 2/2 and 1/1 memory terms with negative z for (a)(c), (a)(d), (b)(c) and (b)(d) across the two backgrounds. That spans reproduced, not reproduced and partial. With no size limit the count is 0 under every reading (cell 19). GO_MIN, GO_MAX = 10, 500 is the author's assumption, not a reading in the claims file (problem 3).
